situation:
You are the financial analyst at MARLOWE RIDGE DEVELOPMENT GROUP, a commercial real estate developer that has built, owned and managed offices, warehouses and extended-stay hotels in one state for twenty years. The chief financial officer (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should finish its first project outside that state, a 140-room extended-stay hotel that is now halfway framed.

Materials and subcontractor labor have risen faster than the nightly rate that market supports, and the gap has eaten most of the project contingency. The company's job-cost ledger and the property system that posts charges to guest folios are separate programs that do not share data, so no one here can yet compare what a finished room costs to build against what that room will earn once the hotel opens.

One course of action is to award the remaining work to the lowest bidder, an out-of-state general contractor the company has never worked with, whose price is far below the others but who will not commit to a completion date. Missing the opening would push the hotel past the booked winter season, and PIEDMONT COAST BANK, which holds the construction loan, raises the rate every month the project runs past its schedule.

The other course of action is to keep the general contractor the company has used at home for fifteen years, who will hold a fixed price and a fixed date. That price consumes what is left of the contingency and the money set aside to connect the two systems, so the hotel would open without the reporting the company counted on and the second out-of-state site would wait a year.

The chief financial officer (judge) wants a recommendation on which course of action to take, what the choice does to the cost of a finished room measured against the rate that room can charge, and how the company should explain the outcome to whoever ends up absorbing it. The chief financial officer (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief financial officer (judge) at MARLOWE RIDGE DEVELOPMENT GROUP. Business background is the same as the situation above.

The company is a regional leader at home and this extended-stay hotel is its first building outside the state. Construction costs are climbing faster than the nightly rate the new market supports, and the contingency that was meant to absorb that is nearly gone. You want to hear which course of action the financial analyst recommends — the lowest bidder who will not commit to a completion date, or the long-time general contractor who will hold a fixed price and a fixed date — and what each one does to the cost of a finished room against the rate that room can charge.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up paying for this decision if it goes wrong?
Is that a fair place for the cost to land?
